relevant_findings.topic: Repaint substrate state is the primary estimation driver
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike NC where substrate state is singular (bare wood), repaint wood siding presents five distinct substrate states: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT, SS_EXT_CHALKING, SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT, SS_EXT_PEELING, SS_EXT_WEATHERED. Each state drives a fundamentally different prep pathway, primer decision, and labor multiplier. The substrate state + substrate condition (DSD 0-4) together form a two-dimensional matrix that is the dominant cost driver for repaint estimation.

relevant_findings.topic: DSD prep multiplier is the dominant cost variable
relevant_findings.finding: MPI Degree of Surface Degradation (DSD) ratings 0-4 drive prep labor multipliers: DSD-0/1 (good) = 1.0-1.25x baseline, DSD-2 (fair) = 1.25-1.5x, DSD-3 (poor) = 1.5-2.0x, DSD-4 (failed) = 3.0x+ or T&M. These multipliers apply to ALL prep tasks and stack multiplicatively with access/height multipliers. Formula: Effective Rate = Baseline Rate / (DM x CM) where DM = deterioration multiplier and CM = complexity/access multiplier.

relevant_findings.topic: Condition assessment is mandatory before estimation
relevant_findings.finding: Repaint estimation cannot proceed without on-site condition assessment. ASTM D3359 tape adhesion testing (ratings 5A-0A) informs both the substrate condition rating and the primer decision. Rating 3A or below requires spot priming at minimum. Rating 1A-0A requires full system removal. Condition assessment is a fixed-time task (per project, not area-scaled).

relevant_findings.topic: Chalking remediation is a distinct prep sequence
relevant_findings.finding: Chalking (UV-degraded resin binder releasing pigment as powder) requires a dedicated remediation protocol: light chalk = low-pressure rinse + soft brush + detergent; moderate = wire brushing or mechanical sanding + high-volume rinse; heavy/severe = controlled pressure washing or abrasive blasting. Post-cleaning verification: hand-rub test and 24-48 hour drying before re-test. If chalk cannot be fully removed, chalk-binding primer (e.g., Loxon Acrylic Conditioner) is mandatory.

relevant_findings.topic: Lead-safe RRP gate for pre-1978 buildings
relevant_findings.finding: Pre-1978 coatings may contain lead. EPA Lead-Safe RRP practices are required before any Class II or Class III paint removal (scraping, sanding, heat gun). RRP is a GATE CONDITION, not a separate spec. When triggered, all prep tasks receive an RRP modifier for containment, HEPA vacuum, wet scraping, and lead-safe disposal. Must evaluate existing coating before disturbing.

relevant_findings.topic: Bond failure classification drives remediation path
relevant_findings.finding: Three failure types: (1) Adhesive — fracture at paint-substrate interface, substrate left bare, caused by surface contamination or low surface energy. (2) Cohesive — fracture within paint film itself, paint residue on both surfaces, caused by over-thinning or excessive thickness. (3) Substrate — substrate material breaks with paint chip (fiber tear on wood), caused by rot or moisture degradation. Substrate failure (type 3) indicates DSD-4 and is outside painting scope. Weak Boundary Layer theory: failures at interface are caused by thin fragile layer (dust, moisture, hydrolytic breakdown) preventing contact.

relevant_findings.topic: Primer selection driven by substrate state
relevant_findings.finding: Sound existing paint: may skip full prime (spot prime bare spots only). Chalking: chalk-binding primer mandatory (Loxon Acrylic Conditioner type). Failing/peeling with <30% bare: spot prime bare areas with acrylic stain-blocking primer. Failing/peeling with >30% bare: full prime required. Weathered bare wood: deep-penetrating oil-alkyd primer to bind loose fibers. Tannin-rich wood (cedar/redwood) exposed: alkyd stain-blocker mandatory regardless of failure extent.

relevant_findings.topic: Cross-grain cracking from excessive paint buildup
relevant_findings.finding: Deep cracking perpendicular to wood grain caused by decades of over-painting. Each successive coat reduces flexibility and vapor permeance. Risk increases with number of existing coats. When cross-grain cracking is present, partial or full strip may be required before recoating. This is a DSD-3+ condition that triggers PCA P14 Level R (restoration) prep. Multiple repaints convert 'breather' coatings into vapor barriers, trapping moisture.

relevant_findings.topic: Moisture blistering vs temperature blistering diagnosis
relevant_findings.finding: Moisture blisters contain liquid water, develop over time, caused by vapor migrating from inside house or entering unsealed joints. Temperature blisters contain air/vapor, appear during/shortly after application, caused by oil-based paint applied in direct sun. Correct diagnosis determines remediation: moisture blisters require moisture source correction (building envelope issue, outside painting scope); temperature blisters require proper application scheduling (SOP concern).

relevant_findings.topic: Siding profile affects repaint production rates
relevant_findings.finding: Profile geometry dramatically affects production rates for both prep and coating. Lap/clapboard: spray 150-250 SF/hr, brush 80-120 SF/hr. Board and batten: spray 120-180 SF/hr, brush 50-70 SF/hr (1.20x effective area multiplier). Shingle/shake: spray 100-150 SF/hr, brush 30-50 SF/hr (highest complexity). Scraping rates on failing paint: 30-60 SF/hr (highly variable by failure severity).

relevant_findings.topic: Extractive bleeding on repaint — tannin management
relevant_findings.finding: On repaint, tannin bleeding (cedar/redwood) reappears when: (1) existing paint has worn thin enough for moisture to reach wood, (2) bare spots expose fresh tannin-rich wood, (3) previous coating system used latex primer instead of alkyd stain-blocker. Run-down streaking = liquid water getting behind siding and washing tannins out through laps (envelope issue). Diffused staining = moisture vapor migrating through weak paint film. All exposed tannin-rich wood must receive alkyd stain-blocker — acrylic primers alone are insufficient for severe tannin staining.

relevant_findings.topic: Power washing constraints on wood siding
relevant_findings.finding: High-pressure washing is discouraged on wood siding — damages springwood, causes 'fuzzy' washboard texture. Appropriate pressure: 500-1000 PSI for wood siding (soft wash), not 2500+ PSI used for masonry. Power wash is for cleaning (dirt, mildew, chalk removal), NOT for paint removal. Paint removal requires mechanical methods (scraping, paint shaver, heat gun).

relevant_findings.topic: DSD-3+ triggers PCA P14 Level R (restoration)
relevant_findings.finding: Severe deterioration (DSD-3) requires complete or near-complete coating removal via abrasion, chemical, or heat methods, plus substrate repair/replacement. This is Restoration-level prep with production rates 50-100% higher than standard prep. DSD-4 (substrate damage — wood rot, structural compromise) is OUTSIDE painting scope entirely. A DSD-4 assessment is a hard stop requiring structural repair before painting can be estimated.

Wood siding MC must be below 15% before coating. Above 20% MC = guaranteed coating failure. Pin-type meter provides point-specific depth readings. Multiple readings across elevations required since moisture varies by exposure. MC verification is a fixed-time task per project, not area-scaled. High MC is a hard stop — cannot proceed until wood dries to acceptable level.

relevant_findings.topic: No back-priming or end-sealing in repaint scope
relevant_findings.finding: Back-priming (coating rear face of siding) and end-sealing (sealing cut ends) are installation-time tasks that cannot be performed once siding is installed. These tasks exist in the NC spec (SF_WOOD_SIDING_EXT_NC_PAINT_v1) only. Repaint addresses only the exposed face of installed siding.
relevant_findings.source: Exterior_Wood_Siding_Systems_Doctrine.md Section 6; NC sibling spec KD-003

relevant_findings.topic: Caulk assessment and replacement in repaint
relevant_findings.finding: Existing caulk at siding-to-trim, siding-to-window, and siding-to-door junctions must be assessed during repaint. Failed caulk must be removed and replaced before coating. This is a prep-phase task unique to repaint (NC caulk is always new). Caulk failure is a common moisture intrusion path that accelerates coating failure on adjacent siding.

condition_drivers.impact: Primary driver of prep pathway, primer selection, and labor scope. Sound paint = minimal prep (wash + light sand). Chalking = chalk remediation + binding primer. Failing = scrape + feather-sand + spot/full prime. Peeling = heavy scrape or strip + full prime. Weathered = sand to fresh wood + oil-alkyd primer. Each state activates different conditional task sets and changes material requirements.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. The substrate state describes the existing coating condition, NOT the level of deterioration (that is substrate_condition). A surface may be SS_EXT_CHALKING + SC_SLIGHT_DETERIORATION (light chalk, mostly sound) or SS_EXT_CHALKING + SC_MODERATE_DETERIORATION (heavy chalk, some peeling). Both dimensions required.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives the DSD prep labor multiplier: SC_SOUND (DSD-0) = 1.0x, SC_SLIGHT (DSD-1) = 1.0-1.25x, SC_MODERATE (DSD-2) = 1.25-1.5x, SC_SEVERE (DSD-3) = 1.5-2.0x, SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE (DSD-4) = 3.0x+ or HARD STOP. DSD-3+ triggers PCA P14 Level R (restoration). DSD-4 is outside painting scope. The multiplier applies to ALL prep tasks and stacks with access multiplier.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE (DSD-4) = rot, structural compromise. This is a HARD STOP — structural repair must occur before painting can be estimated. Do NOT include DSD-4 in production rate calculations — it triggers scope exclusion.

condition_drivers.impact: QT2: economy — power wash, minimal scrape, single finish coat on primed/sound surface. QT3: standard — full wash, scrape and feather, dedicated prime where needed, two finish coats, clean transitions. QT4: premium — TSP wash, thorough scrape/fill/sand, premium primer, two premium finish coats, raking light inspection between coats.
condition_drivers.notes: QT5 not applicable to siding wall field — reserved for fine exterior millwork. QT2 starts at repaint (unlike NC which may start at QT3). QT2 may accept single finish coat on sound primed surface.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives production rate selection and effective area multiplier. Lap is the baseline profile. Board and batten multiplies flat SF by 1.20 for effective paintable area. Shingle has the highest geometric complexity and lowest production rates. Profile also affects scraping difficulty — shingle edges are extremely labor-intensive to scrape.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. Same as NC sibling spec. Profile impacts both prep and coating rates.

condition_drivers.impact: Spray_backbrush is the primary method for siding field (spray followed by backbrushing for fiber penetration). Brush_roll for smaller areas or occupied-adjacent. Brush only for shingle/shake profiles and detail areas. Spray on wood always requires backbrushing — there is no spray-only option.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. Same method set as NC sibling. Spray_backbrush requires 2-person crew. Method affects protection zone escalation (spray = more masking).

condition_drivers.impact: Height modifier on all tasks at elevation. ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. Applied per elevation based on working height. CRITICAL: access multiplier STACKS with DSD prep multiplier. Example: DSD-2 (1.5x) on scaffold (1.60x) = effective 2.4x multiplier on prep tasks.
condition_drivers.notes: Treated as a HEIGHT MODIFIER (like FAC_HEIGHT for interior), not a site condition. Multiplicative stacking with DSD multiplier is the primary repaint cost escalation mechanism.

condition_drivers.impact: Pre-1978 buildings trigger EPA Lead-Safe RRP requirements for all paint removal activities. Adds containment setup/teardown, wet scraping methods, HEPA vacuum, lead-safe waste disposal. RRP modifier applies to all prep tasks involving paint disturbance. Estimated 1.3-1.5x labor premium on affected prep tasks plus material costs for containment supplies.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a GATE CONDITION. Building year is the trigger — if pre-1978, RRP applies regardless of whether lead is actually present (unless testing proves otherwise). RRP is a modifier on this spec's prep tasks, NOT a separate spec.

quality_differences.description: Economy repaint. Power wash only (no TSP). Scrape obvious loose paint. No feather-sanding. Spot prime bare areas. Single finish coat on sound/primed surface. Economy-grade 100% acrylic exterior.
quality_differences.typical_use: Rental property, budget-constrained, pre-sale cosmetic refresh. Only appropriate on SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT or SS_EXT_CHALKING with SC_SOUND/SC_SLIGHT.

quality_differences.description: Standard residential repaint. Power wash with detergent or TSP. Scrape all loose paint. Feather-sand edges. Caulk assessment and replacement. Spot prime or full prime based on substrate state. Two finish coats with mid-grade 100% acrylic. Clean transitions at trim interfaces.
quality_differences.typical_use: Standard homeowner repaint. Handles SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT through SS_EXT_PEELING at SC_SOUND through SC_MODERATE.

quality_differences.description: Premium repaint. Full TSP wash. Thorough scrape, fill, and sand. All caulk replaced. Premium primer where needed. Two finish coats with premium materials (SW Duration, BM Aura). Raking light inspection between coats. Filling nail holes and surface defects to smooth.
quality_differences.typical_use: High-end residential. Handles all substrate states through SC_SEVERE (DSD-3 = PCA P14 Level R restoration prep at this tier).

failure_modes.name: Painting over chalky surface
failure_modes.description: Chalking residue is a primary bond-breaker. If painted over without proper remediation, the new coating bonds to chalk powder rather than sound substrate. Entire new paint system peels as a sheet within months — catastrophic waste of all applied labor and material.
failure_modes.prevention: Complete chalk removal via cleaning hierarchy (rinse -> brush -> mechanical sand -> pressure wash). Verify removal with hand-rub test. If 100% removal impossible without substrate damage, apply chalk-binding primer (Loxon Acrylic Conditioner). Do NOT apply standard primer over chalk.
failure_modes.detection: New paint peeling in large sheets. White powder visible behind detached film. Tape test (ASTM D3359) yields 0A-1A ratings.

failure_modes.name: Inadequate scraping before recoat
failure_modes.description: Painting over failing or peeling paint without removing loose material. New coating bridges over detached existing paint, creating a false bond. Existing paint continues to fail and takes new coating with it. Common shortcut on budget jobs that leads to callback and full redo.
failure_modes.prevention: Scrape ALL loose and flaking paint. Feather-sand edges of sound paint to prevent visible mapping. ASTM D3359 adhesion test at 3+ locations. Spot prime all bare wood exposed by scraping.
failure_modes.detection: Peeling within 6-12 months of repaint. New paint lifts with old paint attached to back. Flaking at original failure boundaries.

failure_modes.name: Extractive bleeding through new coat
failure_modes.description: Tannin-rich wood (cedar, redwood) bleeds water-soluble extractives through new paint film when moisture contacts bare wood. Run-down streaking from laps where water gets behind siding. Diffused brown/tan staining through thin or compromised paint areas.
failure_modes.prevention: All exposed tannin-rich wood must receive alkyd stain-blocking primer — acrylic primers insufficient for severe tannin. Verify no moisture intrusion paths behind siding. End-grain and lap joints are highest risk areas.
failure_modes.detection: Brown/tan streaks or diffuse discoloration appearing weeks to months after painting. Staining worsens after rain events. Most visible on white and light-colored finishes.

failure_modes.name: Cross-grain cracking from excessive paint buildup
failure_modes.description: Deep cracking perpendicular to wood grain caused by decades of over-painting. Each successive coat adds thickness, reduces flexibility, and decreases vapor permeance. Eventually the rigid paint system cannot flex with wood's seasonal expansion/contraction and fractures across the grain.
failure_modes.prevention: Assess existing coat thickness (DFT gauge). If cross-grain cracking is present, partial or full strip required — cannot simply recoat over cracked system. Maintenance coats should be applied thin to avoid continued buildup.
failure_modes.detection: Deep cracks running perpendicular to wood grain direction. Multiple visible paint layers in crack cross-section. May reveal bare wood at crack bottoms.

failure_modes.name: Moisture blistering from envelope failure
failure_modes.description: Interior moisture vapor migrates through wall assembly and pushes paint film off exterior siding. Blisters contain liquid water and develop over time (distinguishing from temperature blisters). Root cause is building envelope issue — missing vapor barrier, bathroom/kitchen exhaust venting into wall cavity, ice dams, missing kick-out flashing.
failure_modes.prevention: Moisture blistering is a building envelope problem OUTSIDE painting scope. Document and report to client. Do not repaint over moisture blisters without addressing moisture source. MC testing before application is mandatory (max 15%, guaranteed failure >20%).
failure_modes.detection: Blisters containing water (puncture test). Progressive development over weeks/months. Concentrated on specific elevations (often bathroom/kitchen side of house). Recurring after previous repaint.

failure_modes.name: Primer incompatibility with existing coating
failure_modes.description: Applying incompatible primer or topcoat over existing system. Oil/alkyd over insufficiently cured latex causes intercoat adhesion failure. Latex directly over glossy oil/alkyd without deglossing or bonding primer causes peeling. Semi-transparent stain cannot accept film-forming paint without bonding primer.
failure_modes.prevention: Identify existing coating type (solvent test: acetone softens latex, not oil/alkyd). Degloss or use bonding primer over glossy oil/alkyd. Do not apply latex directly over glossy surface. Verify stain type before overcoating.
failure_modes.detection: Peeling in sheets along old/new coating boundary. Peeled paint shows clean separation (no substrate fiber). Concentrated at brush marks and roller edges where new coating is thickest.

notes_for_materials_manager: Primer selection is SUBSTRATE STATE-DRIVEN, not tier-driven: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT = spot prime only (acrylic stain-blocking). SS_EXT_CHALKING = chalk-binding primer (Loxon Acrylic Conditioner or equivalent). SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT/SS_EXT_PEELING = acrylic stain-blocking primer (spot or full based on bare area %). SS_EXT_WEATHERED = deep-penetrating oil-alkyd primer.

Tannin-rich wood species (cedar, redwood) with any exposed bare wood OVERRIDE the default primer selection to alkyd stain-blocker. This is a hard blocker rule — acrylic primer alone is insufficient for severe tannin staining. Knot spot-priming with shellac/oil-based may also be needed.

Topcoat: 100% acrylic latex exterior in all cases. Acrylic is superior to alkyd for wood siding — retains flexibility for wood expansion/contraction, resists cracking. Standard system: 2 finish coats (QT3/QT4). QT2 may accept single finish coat on sound primed surface.

Coverage rates for repaint are LOWER than NC due to surface irregularity from previous coating: smooth lap 300-350 SF/gal (vs 350-400 NC), textured/rough 200-300 SF/gal. Primer coverage on scraped/bare spots: 300-400 SF/gal.

Caulk for joint replacement: polyurethane (Class 25/50) or hybrid MS polymer for wood-to-trim joints. Siliconized acrylic acceptable for low-movement joints. Must be paintable. Replace all failed existing caulk.
Scraping tools: carbide hand scrapers, HEPA-equipped paint shavers (for DSD-2+). Heat gun for heavy buildup removal (DSD-3). Chemical stripper for restoration-level work.

Lead-safe RRP materials (when pre-1978): 6-mil poly sheeting for ground containment, HEPA vacuum bags, wet scraping supplies, lead test kits, lead-safe waste bags. These are conditional materials triggered by building age.
Masking tape for wood siding: standard blue tape (14-day) for brush/roll, red stucco poly tape (7.0 mil, 30-day UV rating) for rough profile or extended spray masking.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module structure: setup -> protect -> assess -> prep -> prime -> apply -> cleanup -> teardown. NOTE: 'assess' module is UNIQUE to repaint — condition assessment and adhesion testing occur BEFORE prep begins.

Condition assessment module includes: visual DSD rating, ASTM D3359 tape adhesion test (3+ locations per elevation), moisture content testing (pin meter, multiple readings), existing coating identification (solvent test), lead paint evaluation (if pre-1978). Assessment results determine which prep tasks activate.

Prep module is CONDITIONAL on substrate state: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT = power wash + light sand. SS_EXT_CHALKING = chalk remediation sequence (clean, verify, re-test, binding primer if needed). SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT = scrape loose + feather-sand + spot prime. SS_EXT_PEELING = heavy scrape or strip + full prime. SS_EXT_WEATHERED = sand to fresh wood + alkyd prime.

DSD multiplier applies to ALL prep tasks as a rate modifier. Engine must read substrate_condition and apply the correct DSD multiplier band: SC_SOUND=1.0x, SC_SLIGHT=1.0-1.25x, SC_MODERATE=1.25-1.5x, SC_SEVERE=1.5-2.0x.

Lead-safe RRP module (conditional, pre-1978 buildings): containment setup (6-mil poly ground cover min 10 ft from building), wet scraping methods, HEPA vacuum after each scraping session, lead-safe waste collection and disposal. RRP is a MODIFIER on prep tasks, not a standalone module — it wraps around existing prep activities.
Power wash for wood siding: 500-1000 PSI ONLY (soft wash). High-pressure (2500+ PSI) damages springwood and creates fuzzy texture. Power wash is for cleaning, NOT paint removal.
Spray on wood siding = ALWAYS add backbrushing labor action. Spray + backbrush forces coating into wood fibers. No spray-only option on wood.

Caulk assessment and replacement is a prep task: inspect all siding-to-trim, siding-to-window, siding-to-door joints. Remove failed caulk, clean joint, apply backer rod if >3/8 inch, apply new caulk. Polyurethane caulk requires 3-7 day cure before painting.
DSD-4 (SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE) = HARD STOP in prep module. Cannot proceed with painting if structural damage (rot, compromised wood) is found. Document and report to client for structural repair scope.
Cross-grain cracking assessment: if present, may require partial or full strip. This escalates to DSD-3 / PCA P14 Level R regardless of other condition assessment results.
notes_for_estimation_engineer: PRIMARY COST DRIVER: DSD prep multiplier x access multiplier = effective prep rate reduction. Example: DSD-2 (1.5x) on ladder (1.35x) = 2.025x multiplier. Baseline scrape rate 50 SF/hr becomes effective 24.7 SF/hr. This stacking is the reason repaint can cost 2-3x more than NC on the same surface.

Production rates for coating (QT3 baseline, ground access): spray_backbrush lap 150-250 SF/hr, spray_backbrush board_and_batten 120-180 SF/hr, spray_backbrush shingle 100-150 SF/hr, brush_roll lap 80-120 SF/hr, brush_roll board_and_batten 50-70 SF/hr, brush shingle 30-50 SF/hr.

Prep task rates (QT3 baseline, DSD-0/1, ground access): power wash 400-600 SF/hr, scrape loose paint 30-60 SF/hr, feather-sand 50-80 SF/hr, spot prime 200-300 SF/hr, full prime spray 300-450 SF/hr, full prime brush 100-150 SF/hr, chalk remediation (light) 200-300 SF/hr, chalk remediation (heavy) 80-120 SF/hr.
Board and batten profile: multiply flat SF by 1.20 for effective paintable area. Apply this multiplier before rate calculation.

DSD multiplier bands applied to prep tasks: SC_SOUND (DSD-0) = 1.0x, SC_SLIGHT (DSD-1) = 1.0-1.25x (use 1.15 midpoint), SC_MODERATE (DSD-2) = 1.25-1.5x (use 1.375 midpoint), SC_SEVERE (DSD-3) = 1.5-2.0x (use 1.75 midpoint).

DSD multiplier does NOT apply to coating (apply) tasks — only to prep tasks. Coating production rate is affected by surface profile and access, but not by previous condition (once prepped, the surface is at baseline).

Fixed-time tasks (per project, not area-scaled): condition assessment 1-2 hrs, moisture testing 0.5-1 hr, lead paint evaluation 0.5-1 hr, scaffold setup/teardown 1.75-2.5 hrs setup + 1.0-1.5 hrs teardown per facade (2-person crew).
Caulk replacement: 75-150 LF/hr for removal + re-application. Estimate LF of caulk joints from perimeter and opening count.

Lead-safe RRP modifier (when triggered): 1.3-1.5x labor premium on all prep tasks involving paint disturbance, plus material costs for containment and disposal. RRP setup/teardown is a fixed-time task per work zone.

Coat system: spot/full prime (state-dependent) + 2 finish coats standard at QT3/QT4. QT2 may use single finish coat. Prime coat is conditional — SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT with good adhesion may skip full prime.
Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun, temp) are EXCLUDED from estimation — they are SOP/process concerns, not estimatable at bid time.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray_backbrush
zones.notes: LF-based — measured along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent. Brush/roll: drop cloth at base. Spray: full tarp width over plantings + spray shield.
Extended overspray reach zone beyond 4 ft. Only needed for airless spray — overspray drift can travel 10-15 ft.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray_backbrush
zones.notes: Adjacent walkways. Brush/roll: drop cloth runners. Spray: full tarp coverage.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray_backbrush
zones.notes: Adjacent patio surfaces. Protection level driven by proximity and application method.
Exterior light fixtures mounted on or adjacent to siding. Bag or tape over fixture.
HVAC condenser units adjacent to siding. Full tarp cover during spray operations.

Vehicles and driveway surfaces adjacent to work area. Repaint work on occupied homes means vehicles may be present — spray overspray on vehicles is a costly liability. Tarp cover or vehicle relocation required.

protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Window and door protection during siding work is NOT this spec's responsibility. Window/door masking (glass, hardware, full unit cover) belongs in the respective window or door spec. If windows/doors are not being painted, their protection is scoped under the window/door spec or a separate protection mobilization. This prevents double-counting and ensures protection responsibility is clear per surface owner.
protection_zones_analysis.repaint_specific_note: Repaint on occupied homes has additional protection considerations vs NC: furniture/items on porches, vehicles in driveways, pet containment areas. Client communication about work zone access is an SOP procedure, not an estimation item.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Soffit underside at eave. Often different color (white/light). Siding terminates at soffit/frieze junction. Separate scope — not included in siding spec.
Frieze board — horizontal trim at siding/soffit and siding/foundation junctions. Often different (trim) color. Separate trim scope.
Corner boards frame siding field. Often different color (accent trim). Siding field terminates at corner board.
Window casing trim around openings. Siding terminates at casing. No cut-in — trim is a separate spec. Window protection responsibility belongs to window spec.
Door casing trim. Same as window casing relationship. Door protection is the door spec's responsibility.
Foundation below siding. Not painted in this scope. Drop cloth protection at grade level.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Siding field has NO edge work requirements. All adjacent surfaces are separate specs (soffit, trim, foundation) or not in scope. Protection relationships only. Siding terminates at trim boards — no wet-edge blending across specs. Window/door protection owned by window/door specs. Identical adjacency map as NC sibling spec.

affected_conditions.notes: Access type drives a HEIGHT MODIFIER on tasks. Applied per elevation based on working height. A project may have ground access on one elevation and scaffold on another. CRITICAL for repaint: access modifier stacks with DSD prep multiplier multiplicatively.

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions are important to the painting PROCESS but are NOT estimatable. They are unpredictable, change daily, and cannot be set as fixed conditions for an estimate. They belong in SOP procedure notes and job-site decision protocols, not in production rate modifiers.

excluded.reason: Unpredictable. Changes hourly. Cannot set a fixed modifier for estimate.
Varies by time of day, sun angle, and season. Not predictable at bid time.
Weather-dependent. Not predictable at bid time.
Varies by elevation and season. Professional painters 'follow the shade' — this is scheduling, not estimation.

valid_input_states.rationale: Repaint spec covers all five existing-coating states for wood siding. Each state drives a different prep pathway, primer decision, and labor scope. SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID and SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI are excluded — stain-over-stain recoating is a separate scope (different product system). SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD is the NC spec's domain.

output_state.rationale: Output state is the new painted finish. Satin is the most common exterior siding sheen. Actual output varies by sheen configuration (flat, satin, semi-gloss).

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Repaint context: adjacent trim may be freshly painted (protect from siding spray overspray) or awaiting its own repaint (light mask sufficient). Unlike NC, trim is rarely bare — it has existing coating.
Soffit at eave junction. If already repainted, light mask. If awaiting repaint, no protection needed.
Foundation wall is typically unpainted. Drop cloth at grade level is handled by landscape/hardscape protection zones.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Previously painted wood siding with coating intact and well-adhered. ASTM D3359 rating 4A-5A.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Power wash to clean (500-1000 PSI). Light sand or liquid sander for adhesion tooth. Spot-prime any bare/thin areas.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Spot prime only — acrylic stain-blocking primer on bare areas. No full prime needed if adhesion test passes.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Easiest repaint scenario. Existing coating provides sound base. Skip full prime if adhesion test passes. Minimal scraping — isolated bare spots only.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Previously painted siding with chalky but adhered coating surface. UV-degraded resin binder releasing pigment as powder.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Chalk remediation: cleaning hierarchy from rinse to mechanical sand to pressure wash. Hand-rub test to verify removal. 24-48 hour drying. Re-test. Prime with chalk-binding primer if complete removal not achieved.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Chalk-binding primer (Loxon Acrylic Conditioner type). Low-viscosity, high-penetration resin that soaks through chalk residue and locks it to stable substrate.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Common on aged latex exterior paint, especially south/west facades with high UV exposure. Minor chalking may be intentional 'self-cleaning' effect — only problematic when excessive. Chalk-binding primer is essential if complete chalk removal would damage substrate.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Previously painted siding with cracking, checking, alligatoring, or localized peeling. ASTM D3359 rating 2A-3A.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Scrape all loose/flaking paint via carbide hand scrapers or HEPA-equipped paint shavers. Feather-sand edges of remaining sound paint. Spot prime bare areas. If >30% bare, full prime required.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Acrylic stain-blocking primer on bare areas. If tannin-rich wood exposed: alkyd stain-blocker mandatory. Full prime if >30% of surface is bare.
exterior_substrate_states.pca_level: PCA P14 Level 2 (Standard) to Level R (Restoration) for DSD-3
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Prep time varies dramatically by failure extent. 10-30% failure = scrape and spot prime. >30% failure = full strip may be more economical. Cross-grain cracking indicates excessive buildup — may require full strip regardless of failure percentage.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Active peeling paint — widespread adhesion failure. ASTM D3359 rating 0A-1A. Large ribbons/flakes detaching.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Heavy scraping. May require heat gun or chemical stripper for heavy buildup. Sand to sound substrate. Full prime required on all bare areas.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Full coverage primer. Acrylic stain-blocking for standard softwoods. Alkyd stain-blocker for tannin-rich wood. Deep-penetrating oil-alkyd if wood surface is degraded.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Most labor-intensive prep state short of DSD-4. Prep scope unpredictable — may escalate to hourly billing at QT4+. RRP required if pre-1978 and paint disturbance > 2 SF on building exterior. Lead-safe containment mandatory if triggered.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Uncoated wood siding that has grayed and oxidized from UV/weather exposure. No existing paint — bare wood with degraded surface fibers.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Wood brightener or oxalic acid wash. Sand to remove gray/UV-degraded surface fibers. Must expose fresh wood for primer adhesion. Full prime required.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Deep-penetrating oil-alkyd primer — binds loose wood fibers best. On tannin-rich species: alkyd stain-blocker is both fiber-binding and tannin-blocking.
exterior_substrate_states.pca_level: PCA P14 Level 2 (Standard) to Level R (Restoration)
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Weathered wood surface fibers lack structural integrity — painting over them without removal causes instant peeling. High-pressure washing is NOT recommended for fiber removal (damages springwood). Sand with 80-120 grit to expose fresh wood. May overlap with areas where original coating has completely failed and weathered away.

exterior_access_type_analysis.treatment: Modifier on tasks, not a site condition. Same concept as FAC_HEIGHT for interior.

scenarios.notes: Single-story siding, first 8 ft. No ladder needed. Baseline rate.
Two-story siding, gable ends, areas above 8 ft. Constant repositioning. Safety overhead.
Large continuous areas above 8 ft. Better than ladder for runs >50 LF. Preferred for heavy prep work at height (scraping, sanding).
Boom/scissor lift for 3+ story or difficult access. Requires firm ground. Rental cost.

exterior_access_type_analysis.repaint_note: Access modifier is especially impactful on repaint because it stacks multiplicatively with DSD prep multiplier. Scaffold is often more cost-effective than ladder for repaint at height because heavy prep work (scraping, sanding, power tool work) requires stable platform.

exterior_environmental_constraints.note: Environmental constraints are documented here for SOP reference but are EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers per established exterior spec convention.

sop_reference_only.go_range: 50-90 degrees F surface temperature for wood
sop_reference_only.note: Below 50: slow cure, adhesion risk. Above 90: flash drying on scraped wood, paint blisters.

sop_reference_only.rule: Surface temp must be >= 5 degrees F above dew point
sop_reference_only.note: Adhesion and blushing risk at marginal conditions.
Test with pin-type meter at multiple locations per elevation.

sop_reference_only.rule: Pre-1978 buildings require EPA Lead-Safe RRP evaluation before any paint disturbance
sop_reference_only.note: Not weather-related but is a gate condition evaluated before work begins.

spray_backbrush_lap.notes: Airless spray + backbrush, smooth lap siding. Higher end for long uninterrupted runs.

spray_backbrush_board_and_batten.notes: Vertical profiles require multiple passes. Effective area = 1.20x net area.

spray_backbrush_shingle.notes: Complex profile, many edges. Backbrush essential for coverage on every shingle edge.

brush_roll_lap.notes: Brush for edges/transitions, roller for field.

brush_roll_board_and_batten.notes: Brush dominant — battens require individual attention.

brush_shingle.notes: Extremely labor-intensive. Each shingle edge requires brush attention.

power_wash_wood.notes: Low pressure (500-1000 PSI). For cleaning, NOT paint removal.

scrape_loose_paint_light.notes: Light scraping, DSD-1. Isolated loose spots on otherwise sound surface.

scrape_loose_paint_moderate.notes: Moderate scraping, DSD-2. 10-30% of surface has failing paint.

scrape_loose_paint_heavy.notes: Heavy scraping, DSD-3. >30% failure. May include heat gun work.

feather_sand.notes: Sanding edges of remaining paint to prevent visible mapping.

sand_weathered_wood.notes: 80-120 grit to remove UV-degraded gray fibers. Orbital or hand sand.

chalk_remediation_heavy.notes: Mechanical sanding or controlled pressure wash. Includes re-test.

spot_prime_brush.notes: Brush primer on bare spots. Rate based on total affected SF, not wall SF.

full_prime_spray_backbrush.notes: Full prime when >30% bare or state requires. Spray + backbrush.

full_prime_brush.notes: Full prime brush application for detail areas or non-spray conditions.

caulk_replace.notes: Remove old caulk + clean joint + apply new. Slower than NC caulking due to removal step.

condition_assessment.notes: Fixed time per project. DSD rating + adhesion testing + MC testing + existing coating ID.

moisture_testing.notes: Pin-type meter, multiple locations per elevation.

lead_evaluation.notes: Lead test kit application at 3+ locations. Pre-1978 buildings only.

rrp_containment_setup.notes: 6-mil poly sheeting ground containment min 10 ft. Per work zone.

rrp_containment_teardown.notes: HEPA vacuum, poly roll-up, lead-safe waste bag.

key_decisions.decision: Combined (full phase_scope). Prime and finish phases have unique task keys within the single spec.
key_decisions.rationale: Repaint wood siding is single-mobilization — same crew assesses, preps, primes, and paints. Each phase (assess, prep, prime, finish) has its own task IDs and module IDs for independent rate tracking.

key_decisions.topic: Substrate state as primary configuration dimension
key_decisions.decision: Include 5 substrate states: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT, SS_EXT_CHALKING, SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT, SS_EXT_PEELING, SS_EXT_WEATHERED.
key_decisions.rationale: Substrate state is the dominant dimension in repaint — it determines which prep tasks activate, which primer is used, and the overall labor scope. This is the fundamental difference from NC (which has a single state: bare wood).

key_decisions.decision: Include SC_SOUND through SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE (DSD 0-4). SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE = hard stop.
key_decisions.rationale: DSD rating drives the prep labor multiplier (1.0x to 3.0x+). This is the dominant COST driver for repaint estimation. DSD-4 (substrate damage = rot, structural compromise) is outside painting scope — hard stop requiring structural repair scope.

key_decisions.decision: EXCLUDED from repaint scope. These are installation-time tasks (NC only).
key_decisions.rationale: Back-priming and end-sealing cannot be performed on installed siding. The rear face and cut ends are inaccessible. These tasks exist only in SF_WOOD_SIDING_EXT_NC_PAINT_v1.

key_decisions.decision: RRP is a gate condition modifier on prep tasks, NOT a separate spec.
key_decisions.rationale: Pre-1978 building age triggers RRP for all paint disturbance activities. RRP adds containment, wet scraping, HEPA vacuum, and disposal overhead as a labor/material modifier on existing prep tasks. Creating a separate RRP spec would fragment the estimation flow.

key_decisions.topic: Condition assessment as mandatory first task
key_decisions.decision: Condition assessment is a REQUIRED fixed-time task before any prep or coating work.
key_decisions.rationale: Repaint cannot be estimated without inspecting existing surface. DSD rating, adhesion testing (ASTM D3359), moisture content, and existing coating identification must be performed before prep tasks can be scoped. This is a fundamental difference from NC.

key_decisions.decision: SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE (DSD-4) = outside painting scope. Hard stop in estimation engine.
key_decisions.rationale: DSD-4 indicates structural damage (wood rot, compromised substrate). Painting over structurally damaged wood is not viable — structural repair/replacement must occur first. This is a scope boundary, not a prep level.

key_decisions.topic: DSD multiplier stacks with access multiplier
key_decisions.decision: Prep labor multipliers stack multiplicatively: Effective Rate = Baseline Rate / (DSD_Multiplier x Access_Multiplier).
key_decisions.rationale: Per Exterior_Weathering_Surface_Assessment_Doctrine.md Section 8. The formula reflects that working at height AND on deteriorated surfaces compounds difficulty. This stacking is the primary cost escalation mechanism for repaint.

key_decisions.decision: Include siding_profile dimension: lap_horizontal, board_and_batten, shingle. Same as NC sibling.
key_decisions.rationale: Production rates vary dramatically by profile for both prep and coating. Board and batten has 1.20x effective area multiplier. Shingle has highest prep complexity (scraping every shingle edge).

key_decisions.decision: NOT this spec's responsibility. Per established exterior spec convention.
key_decisions.rationale: Window/door protection belongs in window/door specs. Prevents double-counting. Clear ownership per surface.

key_decisions.decision: EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers. Per established exterior spec convention.
key_decisions.rationale: Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time. They are SOP/process concerns, not estimatable. Same as NC sibling and all exterior specs.

key_decisions.decision: Conditional prime (state-dependent) + 2 finish coats standard at QT3/QT4. QT2 may accept single finish coat.
key_decisions.rationale: Prime is conditional on substrate state — sound paint may skip full prime. Two topcoats provide proper DFT and film build. Exterior coatings need film build from 2 proper coats for durability.

QT2 is appropriate for budget repaint on sound surfaces. QT5 is reserved for fine exterior millwork, not siding field surfaces. This matches the NC sibling but starts at QT2 instead of QT3 (QT2 repaint = minimal prep on sound surfaces).

key_decisions.decision: SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID and SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI excluded from this spec.
key_decisions.rationale: Stain recoating is a fundamentally different product system (stain-over-stain or stain-to-paint conversion). Semi-transparent stain cannot accept paint directly — requires bonding primer and is a separate scope decision. Solid stain-to-paint conversion is possible but has unique compatibility requirements. A separate stain spec or stain-to-paint conversion spec would be more appropriate.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Repaint requires the existing coating state as a primary configuration dimension. NC specs do not need this key (single state). Per-elevation if conditions differ across the building.
proposed_new_keys.notes: Must be set per elevation or per section if substrate state varies across the building.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: DSD rating drives the prep labor multiplier. Must be captured at estimation input. SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE triggers hard stop.
proposed_new_keys.notes: Per-elevation. SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE (DSD-4) triggers scope exclusion alert — painting cannot proceed without structural repair.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Triggers EPA Lead-Safe RRP requirements for all prep tasks involving paint disturbance. Building age is the gate — if pre-1978, RRP applies unless lead testing proves absence.
proposed_new_keys.notes: Project-level flag. Drives RRP modifier on all prep tasks in this spec and any other repaint spec on the project.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Siding profile drives production rate selection and effective area multiplier. Board and batten = 1.20x effective area.
proposed_new_keys.notes: May also be needed by NC sibling spec if not already proposed there.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Repaint on occupied homes may require vehicle/driveway protection from spray overspray. Not typically needed for NC (unoccupied construction site).
proposed_new_keys.notes: SF-based protection area. Optional — only when work zone is adjacent to driveway with vehicles.

research_corrections.original_claim: Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun exposure, surface temperature) should be estimation modifiers
research_corrections.corrected_to: Environmental conditions are NOT estimatable. They are unpredictable at bid time and belong in SOP/process documentation, not production rate modifiers. Removed from estimation scope. Per established exterior spec convention.
research_corrections.corrected_by: Spec Researcher Agent (per established doctrine pattern)

research_corrections.original_claim: Landscape and hardscape protection is SF-based
research_corrections.corrected_to: Landscape perimeter protection is LF-based (measured along house perimeter). Hardscape walk/patio remains SF-based. Per Protection_Zones_Reference.md and established exterior spec pattern (masonry spec uses PS_EXT_PROTECT_LF.LANDSCAPE_PERIMETER).
research_corrections.corrected_by: Spec Researcher Agent (aligned with masonry sibling)

research_corrections.original_claim: Substrate condition modifier should be excluded from estimation (as in NC)
research_corrections.corrected_to: Substrate condition modifier IS INCLUDED in repaint estimation. DSD prep multiplier is the core of repaint cost estimation — it drives the prep labor multiplier from 1.0x to 3.0x+. This is the opposite of NC where substrate condition is singular (bare) and not a variable. Condition assessment IS the estimatable dimension for repaint.
research_corrections.corrected_by: Spec Researcher Agent (per user brief RC-003)

research_corrections.original_claim: DSD-4 (substrate damage) should have a prep multiplier like other DSD levels
research_corrections.corrected_to: DSD-4 (SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE) = outside painting scope. This is a HARD STOP, not a prep level. Structural repair (rot replacement, wood reinforcement) must occur before painting can be estimated. Do not include DSD-4 in production rate tables — it triggers scope exclusion.
research_corrections.corrected_by: Spec Researcher Agent (per user brief RC-004, Exterior_Weathering_Surface_Assessment_Doctrine.md Section 5)

research_corrections.original_claim: Lead-safe RRP should be a separate spec
research_corrections.corrected_to: Lead-safe RRP is a gate condition, not a separate spec. RRP is a modifier that applies to all prep tasks when building is pre-1978. It wraps around existing prep activities with containment, wet methods, and disposal overhead. Creating a separate spec would fragment the estimation flow.
research_corrections.corrected_by: Spec Researcher Agent (per user brief RC-005)

research_corrections.original_claim: Back-priming and end-sealing should be included in repaint spec
research_corrections.corrected_to: Back-priming and end-sealing are EXCLUDED from repaint. These are installation-time tasks that cannot be performed once siding is installed. They exist in the NC spec (SF_WOOD_SIDING_EXT_NC_PAINT_v1) only.

assumptions.value: Repaint of existing wood siding — condition-dependent prep and coating. Exterior wall field surfaces only.
assumptions.note: Trim, windows, doors, soffit are separate specs. Foundation is separate. This spec covers only the siding field surface.

assumptions.value: Stain substrate states (SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID, SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI) excluded from this spec
assumptions.note: Stain recoating and stain-to-paint conversion are separate scopes with unique material and compatibility requirements.

assumptions.value: QT5 not applicable to siding wall field applications
assumptions.source: Sibling spec pattern (NC wood siding, masonry)
assumptions.note: QT5 reserved for fine exterior millwork, columns, decorative elements. Not wall field surfaces.

assumptions.value: SC_SUBSTRATE_DAMAGE (DSD-4) is outside painting scope — hard stop requiring structural repair
assumptions.note: DSD-4 indicates rot, structural compromise. Cannot be addressed by painting — requires carpentry/contractor scope.

assumptions.value: Lead-safe RRP is a modifier on prep tasks, not a separate spec. Triggered by building year (pre-1978).
assumptions.note: RRP adds containment, wet methods, HEPA vacuum, and disposal overhead. Estimated 1.3-1.5x labor premium on affected tasks.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine provides multiplier ranges per DSD level (e.g., 1.25-1.5x for DSD-2) but not exact production-calibrated values. Using midpoints as defaults (1.15 for DSD-1, 1.375 for DSD-2, 1.75 for DSD-3).
uncertainties.recommendation: Field calibration with timed prep data across DSD levels to narrow midpoint values.

uncertainties.detail: Scraping rates range from 15-100 SF/hr depending on DSD level, siding profile, existing coat thickness, and whether paint is latex or oil. This 6.7x variance makes scraping the hardest task to estimate precisely.
uncertainties.recommendation: Stratify scraping rates by DSD level and profile (e.g., DSD-2 lap vs DSD-3 shingle). Consider T&M fallback for DSD-3+ scraping.

uncertainties.detail: RRP adds significant overhead (containment, wet methods, HEPA, disposal) but the exact labor premium is not precisely documented in doctrine. Estimated 1.3-1.5x based on industry experience.
uncertainties.recommendation: Field calibration with timed RRP vs non-RRP prep on similar DSD conditions.

uncertainties.topic: Mixed substrate states on same building
uncertainties.detail: A single building may have different substrate states on different elevations (e.g., north side = sound paint, south side = chalking, west side = peeling). The estimation engine must support per-elevation substrate state assignment.
uncertainties.recommendation: PS_EXT_META.ENUM.SUBSTRATE_STATE and PS_EXT_META.ENUM.SUBSTRATE_CONDITION should support per-elevation values, not just project-level.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine indicates >30% bare area triggers full prime vs spot prime, but the threshold is approximate and field judgment applies. Some contractors use 25% or 40% as their threshold.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use 30% as default threshold. Allow estimator override.
